title: ready-03: sessions — palette `#` mode, CLI, plain `heca` attaches to the last one
summary: Named sessions, same-window # switching, GUI/CLI actions, explicit terminate/restart/delete with distinct client behavior.
description:
Third step of the server/client model. Depends on P099 (the connection). F012 accepted decision "Sessions: palette # mode, CLI flags, plain heca attaches to the last session, saved as JSON". Replaces the earlier plan of one process per instance with OS window switching.

## Goal
- The server holds many sessions, each with a name and a project folder (heca-pro stores its linked feature on it).
- **Palette `#` mode** beside `:` commands, `@` panes, `$` workspaces: one row per session (name, folder, windows attached, agents running); picking one switches this window; searchable and remembered.
- P100/T526 already delivered one palette mode table. Reuse it for # and preserve existing mode search history.
- Actions: new, rename, terminate, restart, delete, detach, switch — in the palette, bindable, callable by RPC.
- CLI (cli.rs flag style): `heca --sessions [--json]`, `--attach <name>`, `--new [path] [--name <name>]`, `--kill <name>`, `--standalone`. Plain `heca`: server running → attach to the last session; none → start the server in the background and attach. P105/T527 supplies restoration of saved sessions after server exit. `--standalone` = today's behaviour.

## Session create + default naming (2026-10-27)
Create flows and default naming agreed with Antonio — the canonical detail is in
`.planner/docs/p100-session-create.md` (owner T522). In short:
- `heca --new [path] [--name <name>]`: path = project folder (omitted → cwd; relative → under cwd; absolute/`~` → that path; created if missing, else used). `--name` optional; settings.session_name_format supplies automatic names (default `heca #{number}`), using the destination project's trusted config over user settings/defaults.
- Palette "Create Session": fuzzy path input (no OS picker); relative paths resolve against the focused pane's cwd; a non-existent path offers an explicit "Create folder: <path>"; folder optional (tmux-like).
- Automatic session names are progressive through settings.session_name_format; explicit rename replaces the entire name.

## Preserve
- Text from wherever the app keeps user-facing text; nothing hard-coded. Not blocked by any other feature.

## Done when
- Two sessions; `#` in the palette lists both and switches in the same window; the CLI lists and attaches; plain `heca` reattaches to the last one.

## Approved Lifecycle (2026-10-27)
Canonical ownership: F012 decisions c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d and 2fc26220-2583-4392-bc2f-4724d406a555.
- Terminate stops processes and retains the session definition and stopped state. Clients remain open with Session unavailable, explicit Restart, existing/new session selection, and Exit.
- Restart is an explicit action. A terminated session must not restart just because a server or client reconnects.
- Delete stops it if active, removes Heca-owned runtime/selection references and keeps affected windows open for existing/new session selection or Exit. Other sessions and project files are untouched.
- Normal GUI launch starts a missing server; existing disconnected windows show the agreed blocking server-unavailable dialog instead of restarting it automatically.
- --kill <name> is termination, not deletion; permanent-delete CLI spelling is still unspecified.
- T522 captures original launch executable/arguments/cwd and native harness session/driver identity. P105/T527 persists these and applies resume_programs=true / resume_harness=true through registered harness CLI capabilities.
- P100 owns live lifecycle and protocol. Persistence, durable deletion and restore after server exit belong to P105; they must not become a circular dependency that prevents T522 completing.

Additional acceptance: several clients observe the correct termination dialog; explicit restart targets the same session; detach/delete leave only affected windows unattached and able to select/create a session or exit; stale references cannot recreate a deleted session. T522 is DONE: its implementation landed on main through PR #304, merge64a89901 (code845848a5), verified in main c3f86ac3. Antonio accepted A/B focus/border/spacing, folder creation/completion and feedback behavior through the v10 review on 2026-11-03. Antonio accepted the final server-loss/explicit reconnect review on 2026-11-04; T522 has12/12 checked. See its current evidence; PR #304 (https://github.com/ovidius72/heca/pull/304) is MERGED into main and all12/12 checks are accepted. The canonical planner closeout is published directly on main per Antonio's instruction.

Disabled resume does not remove or disable a pane: its own registered content starts fresh with its normal configured defaults. Terminal programs/harnesses become a normal shell, browser uses its default home, editor has no open files. This is generic for future registered content; T527 consumes existing managed-content factory/lifecycle ownership, without a closed content-kind list.

Protocol ownership: F012 decision 2534270c-efd4-46ed-91ee-ddcd620b69b6. T522 owns session-select/attach. T545 owns sizing/follow/titles within a selected session. Both use one server-assigned Connection.id, one receive/pump stamping point and the existing ClientMsg/ServerMsg protocol; no duplicate client identity.

## T522 Feedback Repair (Revised 2026-10-29)
T522 also owns the approved pane-feedback repair in its existing worktree. The task's Accepted Decision 'Pane feedback is suppressed only by effective focus in the active window' is the contract: retain actual command/program completion success/error and configured integration attention events; suppress the local flash only for the actual input-focused pane in the active window. The later T522 decision 'Pane feedback repeats gently with a configurable timeout and one sound per event' requires gentle repeats until acknowledgement or settings.notification_flash milliseconds (0 endless), with at most one configured sound attempt per revision across clients. Session-owned revisions and acknowledgement are shared across clients. No program allowlist or duration threshold. T522 records automated tests and Antonio's native acceptance separately; implementation is now verified merged through PR #304.
Confirmed defaults: notification_flash=8000ms (eight seconds), 0 remains endless, notification_sound=true controls feedback sound for all programs. The flash must use the pane row's configured radius. T522 fixed an extra self-clip that cut the renderer's outer stroke; regression verifies matching geometry at several radii. Antonio accepted the feedback and border visually on 2026-10-29; the final remaining T522 native acceptance was completed on 2026-11-04.

T522 presentation follow-ups (2026-11-03): the folder picker reuses fuzzy matching with its own case-insensitive default (folder_search_case), including capitalized Tab completion. The shared pane-name projection filters brief commands using pane_name_delay=1000ms (0 immediate); runtime facts and feedback remain immediate. These are task-owned decisions and accepted UI repairs, not persistence work. Server replacement/reused-ID and missing-session reconnect tests pass against the real owner loop. Antonio accepted native reconnect in an isolated fixture on 2026-11-04, observing NEW SERVER A > and pwd ending projects/A. Only the approved test server was stopped; unrelated servers were untouched. Seeded replacement sessions are not T527 disk restoration.

Session confirmation update (2026-11-03): F012 lifecycle decision c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d requires distinct default-on Terminate/Delete prompts, Cancel first, configured wording and independent [confirm] toggles. --kill asks [y/N] (2026-11-04 refinement), using the same spec and target-project configuration; missing/negative input never terminates. T522 implements this through the existing action and CLI dispatcher metadata, not call-site dialogs. All13 real server/native tests and broad tests/clippy pass; Antonio confirmed the supplied manual confirmation flow works on 2026-11-04; the final reconnect review was also accepted on 2026-11-04. The v11 current-terminated-picker and stationary-pointer fixes were accepted by Antonio. C7/C12 are checked; T522 is12/12 verified. Antonio merged PR #304 (code845848a5, merge64a89901); T522 is DONE and P100 derives DONE from its completed tasks. Tests/clippy/rustdoc and13 explicit native/socket tests passed; PR excludes planner/graphify/runtime files. Merge is verified; T527 still owns disk restoration. Runtime-safe worktree cleanup is separate from completed phase behavior. Verified tasks must be DONE before future code PRs and canonical planner updates must be committed/pushed on main, as corrected by Antonio on 2026-11-04.

tasks.title: Sessions in the server: palette `#` mode, session actions, CLI, plain `heca` attaches to the last
tasks.description:
Execution task for P100 — read the phase and F012's decision "Sessions: palette # mode…" first. Depends on P099 (connection) and on the mode-table task in this phase (do that first). Replaces the old OS window-switching plan: no per-OS focus hand-over is needed any more.

Approved 2026-10-27 (F012 decisions c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d and 2fc26220-2583-4392-bc2f-4724d406a555):
- Keep distinct actions for terminate, restart and delete, alongside new, rename, detach and switch, through the existing catalog, GUI, bindings and RPC.
- Terminate stops session processes and retains its definition with a stopped state. Affected clients stay open with Session unavailable, [Restart], existing/new session selection, and [Exit]. Do not switch or restart automatically.
- Restart is explicit and rebuilds the retained session. Delete stops it if active, removes Heca-owned live references, and leaves affected windows open for existing/new session selection or Exit. Do not delete project files or affect another session.
- --kill <name> terminates the session; it is not permanent deletion. Permanent-delete CLI spelling remains unspecified; do not invent it.
- Capture original executable, structured arguments and working directory; retain registered harness driver identity and the native harness session ID. Never substitute a Heca session ID or PID.
- config.toml resume_programs=true and resume_harness=true are independent category defaults. P105/T527 owns durable JSON and policy-driven relaunch/resume through each harness's CLI API, not a universal --sessionId.
- Runtime lifecycle/state/launch capture belong here. Disk persistence, durable deletion and post-server-restart recovery belong to T527, which depends on this task; do not create a circular prerequisite.
- Preserve one socket/in-process code path, normal GUI auto-start of a missing server, same-window switching, other clients' attachment, and standalone behavior.

## Session create + default naming (2026-10-27)
Create flows and default naming agreed with Antonio — canonical detail in `.planner/docs/p100-session-create.md`:
- `heca --new [path] [--name <name>]`: path = project folder (omitted → cwd; relative → under cwd; absolute/`~` → that path; created if missing, else used); `--name` optional; the default comes from settings.session_name_format, whose default is `heca #{number}`.
- Palette "Create Session": fuzzy path input, no OS picker; a relative path resolves against the focused pane's cwd (fallback home); a non-existent path offers an explicit "Create folder: <path>"; the folder is optional (tmux-like — with none the session starts on a default and you navigate).
- Default session names use settings.session_name_format (`heca #{number}` by default), loaded from the destination project's trusted configuration over user settings/defaults. The number distinguishes automatic names; explicit rename replaces the whole name.
- The window title (`path` + ` #k` from the second window on the same instance) is built in P099/T545; keep the naming consistent with it.

Edge cases: duplicate names; unknown attach gives a clear message and offers creation; last session terminated/deleted; several windows on one session; reconnect after server stop; terminated sessions never auto-resurrect. When resume is disabled, preserve the pane and initialize its own registered content's fresh default: a terminal-hosted program/harness becomes a normal shell; a browser uses its configured home page; an editor has no files open. This is an open factory/lifecycle contract for all future content, not a closed enum or a universal Terminal fallback. T527 consumes it; P094/T452 and P067/T398 retain ownership of the shared content factory foundations.

## Protocol Agreement With T545
Canonical F012 decision 2534270c-efd4-46ed-91ee-ddcd620b69b6 (Antonio + Opus, 2026-10-27).
T522 owns session selection and the attach handshake. Preserve the existing server-assigned Connection.id as the sole client/window identity: allocate once per connection, never per selection or in the client. Maintain one receive/pump stamping point and pass that ID down to process input/resize. Reuse the same ClientMsg/ServerMsg enums. Give T545 an already attached client/session and this same ID; do not reimplement its size arbitration, follow or title policy. Keep ServerLoop as the owner-loop entry while isolating session state.

## Feedback Repair Included By Antonio (2026-10-28)
Antonio explicitly requires this fix in T522 and the existing heca-p100 worktree, not a new task/worktree. T551 was canceled without source changes and its empty worktree/branch removed. T398 supplied a proposal; do not assume another agent implemented the correction. Reuse local FlashHandle only for painting. Server session owns pane feedback_revision / seen_through_revision and semantic status; pending iff feedback_revision > seen_through_revision. Acknowledge through the one client/server protocol, scoped to the sender's selected session; stale/repeat acknowledgements must not erase newer events. Snapshot current pending/seen state on attach. Revised by Antonio on 2026-10-29: actual command/program completions, including ordinary shell commands and editors, create success/error feedback. Do not add a program allowlist or duration threshold. Enabled registered integrations also supply their configured meaningful semantic events. Suppress the local pulse only for the pane with actual input focus in the active OS window; an inactive window's selected pane does not count. Initialization, work/tool progress, compaction, subagents, deliberate interruption, metadata/repaint/reconnect/replay do not create feedback. Do not infer new events from runtime snapshots; preserve one-shot backend completion alerts. No driver-name list in dock. Effective focus requires an active OS window and actual pane input focus, not merely selection under an overlay/palette/dock. Already-focused panes acknowledge automatically. Revised by Antonio on 2026-10-29: background feedback repeats gentle theme-owned pulses until shared acknowledgement or settings.notification_flash milliseconds; 0 means endless. Active input-focused panes do not flash. A new eligible background revision requests one configured sound; the server grants at most one client an attempt, so pulses and multiple windows do not duplicate it. Expiry stops the animation without acknowledging feedback. See the task's accepted decision 'Pane feedback repeats gently with a configurable timeout and one sound per event'. Ack in one window clears attention in all without altering agent status. Regression coverage includes ordinary ls/git status/false in active/background, two-client ack, revision race, reconnect, rebuild/theme and overlay focus. Correct obsolete README integration-CLI statement and distinguish explicit installation/enabling, updates preserving user choices and independent sounds.

Approved settings, 2026-10-29: settings.notification_flash defaults to 8000ms (0 endless); settings.notification_sound defaults true for feedback from all programs. The generic sound boolean replaces the agent-only enable flag. Startup/reload use the same settings mapping. Antonio accepted the feedback and border visually; remaining composite C12 checks must be verified separately.

Approved continuation 2026-11-02: logical Detach removes this window from session membership without closing the connection or stopping programs. Detach, Terminate and Delete all offer existing session, new session, and Exit. Exit closes the window, not a second Detach loop. Extend the shared CommandPalette with optional candidate completion for Tab; keep filesystem resolution and explicit new-folder creation in the existing session folder source. C2 was accepted by Antonio on 2026-11-03: A/B switching restores the focused pane without border or spacing regressions.
Preflight: reuse CommandPalette/source, Input, shared ModalSpec/Dialog and existing registered session actions; inventories docs/widgets.md, components and chrome surfaces checked. No PathInput/autocomplete widget currently exists, so generic candidate completion belongs in CommandPalette under approved T522 scope. No new task or one-off event path.

## Reviewed Presentation Follow-ups (2026-11-03)
Antonio accepted new-folder creation, fuzzy case-insensitive folder completion after Tab, active-pane silence/background feedback, shared two-window acknowledgement and delayed pane program names. Folder pickers use settings.folder_search_case=insensitive independently of search_case. Pane names use one shared typed presentation with settings.pane_name_delay=1000ms (0 immediate); raw process/agent/status facts and feedback are not delayed. Canonical name policy is this task's Accepted Decision 2b9968f9-696e-46f0-a571-fd36af028f95. No program allowlist or feedback duration threshold is introduced.

Current acceptance: 12/12 verified and accepted by Antonio on 2026-11-04. Code commit845848a5 landed through PR #304 (https://github.com/ovidius72/heca/pull/304), merged as64a89901 and present in main c3f86ac3. Explicit reconnect selected the intended renamed session despite B reusing its prior numeric ID and being last-used. The window stayed open without auto-start, then displayed NEW SERVER A > and pwd ending projects/A. Missing names fail without fallback creation. These seeded sessions are not T527 JSON/process/layout restoration. T545 can now consume the merged attach contract from main. Canonical task/phase/feature completion and verification evidence must be committed and pushed from /Users/antonio/projects/heca on main; they must not remain only local or in this feature worktree.

## Session Confirmations (Approved 2026-11-03)
F012 lifecycle decision c205c5f5-cd0a-4212-9fda-8a8c63c98d3d now requires default-on, distinct Terminate/Delete pre-action confirmations with Cancel initially selected and the concrete target named. Reuse action-owned ConfirmSpec and the existing ModalSpec/Dialog; warning text/buttons come from settings.session_text, independent boolean overrides from [confirm].terminate_session and [confirm].delete_session. Detach stays unprompted. --kill also asks textually using the same spec/config: the central CLI dispatcher enforces declarative command metadata, target-session project config is loaded before prompting, and only y/Y proceeds in the approved [y/N] prompt (2026-11-04); n/N or Enter cancels. Blank, EOF, unknown input or I/O failure never terminates. RPC without an answerable prompt fails closed. Implemented here and covered by real GUI/action/socket/CLI tests; Antonio confirmed the supplied manual confirmation flow works on 2026-11-04. Antonio then accepted the final server-loss/reconnect review on 2026-11-04; all 12 checklist items are verified. PR #304 is merged into main. Antonio requested T522 DONE; the canonical planner must be published on main. The corrected workflow marks verified tasks DONE before opening their code PR, rather than waiting for merge. Runtime-safe worktree cleanup is separate from completed implementation. This does not change T527 persistence ownership or the T545 merge order.

acceptedDecisions.title: T522/T545 concrete attach, window directory and follow contract
acceptedDecisions.decision: Connection.id is the sole client/window identity, assigned once per physical connection by the server at the single receive/pump point. Switching sessions on that connection preserves the id; a new connection receives a new id. T522 owns selection, attach, and per-session presentation ordinal allocation. T545 owns size arbitration, client-side title formatting, the session window directory, title reports, and follow. The user selects a follow target by its displayed title; the stored/transmitted target is Connection.id, so renaming does not break follow. Both tasks extend the same ClientMsg/ServerMsg protocol. Merge T522 before T545's attach-dependent follow/title integration; T545 follow/title integration (C4/C5) waits for T522 merged into main, without sharing an intermediate T522 branch. T522 delivers session selection, attach metadata and ordinal allocation. Do not implement T545 title formatting, directory or follow.
acceptedDecisions.rationale: Confirmed with Opus on 2026-10-28; extends F012 Accepted Decision 2534270c-efd4-46ed-91ee-ddcd620b69b6 and keeps both agents on one protocol.
acceptedDecisions.implementationNotes:
T522/T545 concrete agreement confirmed with Opus on 2026-10-28. This is an integration contract, not a claim of merged implementation. On Opus's reported main base af4fff24, Attached has content only. SessionInfo/session selection are unmerged T522 work in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-p100 on feat/p100-sessions.

Final T522 data shape: SessionInfo { id: heca_core::layout::SessionId, name: String, folder: Option<std::path::PathBuf>, label: Option<String>, status: SessionStatus, windows: usize, agents: usize }. SessionId already exists as SessionId(pub u64); SessionStatus is Active or Terminated. Reuse session.id and session.folder without duplicate identities or path fields.

T522 will deliver ServerMsg::Attached { session: SessionInfo, client_id: u64, window_ordinal: u64, content: SessionContent }. SessionInfo is already in the T522 worktree; client_id/window_ordinal are still pending there when this agreement is recorded. Preserve server::run::ServerLoop as the owner-loop entry with session state isolated.

T522 assigns ordinals from 1 using one per-session server-owned counter when a connection joins that session. Ordinals are presentation numbers, not client identities. They remain stable for that attachment; gaps are allowed, and leaving does not renumber others. Restart/republication of Attached for the same attached client/session must preserve its ordinal. A session switch preserves Connection.id but obtains the destination session's ordinal. No promise of cross-server-restart identity persistence is introduced.

T545 formats each window title client-side from folder and ordinal; ordinal 1 has no suffix, ordinal > 1 has the agreed #k suffix. Formatting/text comes from the owning configuration. T545 owns the shared WindowInfo { id: u64, ordinal: u64, title: String }, ServerMsg::Windows { session_id: SessionId, windows: Vec<WindowInfo> }, and a ClientMsg reporting the sender window's title. The server attributes reports to the stamped Connection.id and selected session, never to a caller-selected window id. Handle stale reports across a session switch without publishing them into the wrong session.

T545 publishes a session-scoped window snapshot after Attached and on join, leave, and title change; a session switch updates both old and new session membership. Follow resolves the displayed title to the authoritative id and retains that id across renames. T522 supplies attachment lifecycle hooks and metadata; T545 owns directory/title/follow behavior. Neither adds another handshake, identity, or transport.

Antonio's integration constraint, 2026-10-28: do not share or base T545 on the unmerged T522 branch. Complete/review T522 and merge it into main first; T545 C4/C5 then starts from that merged main. Opus checked main af4fff24 and reports no clean independent follow/title implementation slice there, so do not tell him C4/C5 can proceed before the T522 attach fields land. Earlier size-arbitration work is separate. No task status, whole-task dependency, or ownership change is implied.

acceptedDecisions.title: Stabilize displayed pane program names without delaying runtime or feedback
acceptedDecisions.decision: Antonio approved a configurable delay for displayed pane names on 2026-11-03, so brief shell commands such as ls/cd do not cause zsh -> command -> zsh flicker.
